sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Basis**: Formed under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**, which proposed an Interim Government with the support of major political parties.
• **Viceroy's Role**: The Viceroy (Lord Wavell, later Lord Mountbatten) remained the **Head of the Executive Council**, but the government functioned as a de facto cabinet.
• **Congress Entry**: Jawaharlal Nehru was designated as the **Vice-President of the Executive Council**, effectively acting as the Prime Minister.
• **League Entry**: The Muslim League joined in October 1946 but maintained a policy of **obstructionism** rather than cooperation.

items.definition: The body that functioned as the Cabinet; members were technically advisors to the Viceroy but acted as ministers of departments.
The 'Poor Man's Budget' presented by the League Finance Minister, designed to target industrialist supporters of the Congress, highlighting the internal rift.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Constituent Assembly**: The Interim Government facilitated the first session of the Constituent Assembly on Dec 9, 1946.
• **Foreign Policy**: Nehru initiated an independent foreign policy, establishing diplomatic relations with the USA and USSR.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Communal riots (Direct Action Day aftermath), administrative paralysis, and lack of unified command.
• **Solutions**: Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947) was the ultimate solution to the deadlock, leading to the Indian Independence Act.

items.title: Mnemonic for Key Portfolios
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'J-L-V-B' (Jawaharlal-Liaquat-Vallabhbhai-Baldev).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Jawaharlal (External Affairs), Liaquat (Finance), Vallabhbhai (Home), Baldev (Defence).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if the Interim Government was a 'Dominion Government'. It was NOT. It was an Executive Council under the 1919 Act framework, not a sovereign cabinet.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Administrative Paralysis' to describe the functioning of the Interim Government due to the League's 'King's Party' approach.

keyTakeaways: The Interim Government was a transitional arrangement under the 1919 Act, not a sovereign body.
The inclusion of the Muslim League was a tactical error that led to administrative deadlock.
The Finance portfolio held by the League was used as a political weapon against Congress-led departments.
